subject: Capacity convergence: temporary autoscale exception and pool reallocation
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lisa Jones <lisa.jones@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity convergence: temporary autoscale exception and pool reallocation

Team —

Quick context: Orion Health (Lisa on copy) is moving their pilot traffic into a limited prod slice next week for a phased launch. They need a short, guaranteed headroom window for two weeks to run customer-facing traffic with our SLOs (p95 latency target and 99.9% availability). Their traffic profile spikes while models warm up; current pilot showed 3x transient token throughput compared to staging distributions.

Ask: can infra approve a temporary autoscale exception + short-term reallocation of one XL GPU slot from the dev-slate pool into a dedicated pilot slice for 14 days (May 10–24)? I attached a short proposal with expected throughput, rollback criteria, and metrics to monitor.

Tradeoffs I'm aware of: this will momentarily reduce dev pool capacity; I propose we throttle non-critical batch runs and notify impacted teams. From sales side, Marissa can confirm revenue/contract notes — Marissa, can we convert this into a short-term commercial addendum if ops approves?

If infra needs a mitigation plan, Marcus / Kimberly — please propose the minimum ops guardrails you'd need (cold-start cooldown, KV cache priming steps, threshold based autoscale revert).

Thanks —
Rishi
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_rebalance_proposal.xlsx, prod-slo-requests.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lisa Jones <lisa.jones@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity convergence: temporary autoscale exception and pool reallocation

Thanks Rishi —

High level: technically feasible, but we need to limit blast radius and codify the revert triggers before we carve out capacity. From an autoscale policy perspective, I want the following in place before we hand over the pilot slice:

- Canary ramp (3 days) with a 50% traffic cap, step-up schedule documented in Drive; if p95 > target for two consecutive 1h windows we roll back.
- Autoscale exception window limited to 14 days and automatically revoked at 2027-05-24 23:59 PDT unless we approve an extension.
- Monitoring hooks: dedicated SRE dashboard (token-level cost, p95, error-rate), Slack alert channel, and an incident playbook link.
- No changes to core hot-restart policies; KV priming script must run during the canary to avoid cold-cache thundering.

Operational constraints: removing one XL slot from dev-slate reduces available concurrent batch slots; please confirm which batch jobs we can suspend. I can provision the slice if Marcus signs off on the gating metrics and we commit to the canary schedule.

I'll pre-populate the incident playbook and share the dashboard link by EOD.

-Kim
Sr. Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Kim — Rishi —

I ran a quick feasibility check against the pool schedules. We can carve one XL slot for the requested window, but a few notes:

- Dependency: we'll need a short freeze on noncritical nightly batch runs for three nights (May 9–11) to pre-warm the KV caches and stage the model weights on the node. That buys more steady-state headroom during peak.
- Network SLAs: the pilot slice will need the same egress priority as production to avoid tail latency from external partners; that requires a temporary QoS rule which networking can deploy with a 4h lead.
- Failure mode: if autoscale doesn't kick fast enough during a burst we will fallback to a lower-quality model variant for up to 30 minutes. We must inform Orion and document that in the addendum.

If Marissa confirms the commercial side and Lisa confirms acceptance of fallback behavior, I can schedule the node carve and push the QoS change.

-Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
